- 2026-09-06 · cowork · K1 CONTRACT CRITIQUE (rebuild/m3/w6/PRODUCTION-DEPENDENCIES.md @ 2ce1008, docs only; reviewed as a CONTRACT PROPOSAL, not an implementation acceptance; T1 / R1 / P1 and the ordinary CLEAN bounded restart stay visible and unwaived; no product waiver, no new owner question raised): the lifecycle (arm → register-before-observe → persist outcome → close, OPEN survives failure, relaunch with an unresolved OPEN is not CLEAN) is the right shape, but the proposal is NOT implementable as written because it does not say what an unresolved obligation MEANS on relaunch per kind, and the one-size answer "18 until re-proven" makes offline use collapse. Minimum missing schema, with the decisive counterexamples: (1) PER-KIND OBLIGATION TABLE — for each finite source {local permission sample; sign-out intent; /op drain request; /pull and /snapshot; /time challenge; token refresh; cross-context join; any remaining SDK/SW event} state the possible negative outcomes (11/17/19/20/18), what is persisted BEFORE any consequence, and the RELAUNCH RESOLUTION when the child is found OPEN without an outcome — CLEAN-with-UNKNOWN, 17, or 18 — with the exposure argument for each. Counterexample A: a set is logged, the drain starts an /op request, the phone loses signal and iOS kills the app in the background; next morning offline in the gym the only durable state is OPEN with an unresolved request child → under the current text 18 → the athlete cannot log until network returns; every kill during an online drain produces this. Counterexample B: the local permission sample happens on EVERY commit; if every sample is a managed observation the app is OPEN whenever it writes and an ordinary kill mid-commit is never CLEAN — the "permanent OPEN-per-session" the proposal itself forbids. Required resolution: classify the local sample as a SELF-CONTAINED observation whose outcome is the frame written in the same transaction (atomic: either the sample and its latch/H/W_last commit together or nothing does), with the explicit exposure argument that a lost local sample is bounded by the remaining allowance the owner already ruled bounded; and classify a request child whose response was NEVER READ as UNOBSERVED → close as UNKNOWN with CLEAN retained (the server bounds that exposure through the lease and later refusals), reserving 18 for children whose response bytes WERE read but whose consequence failed to persist. Because a kill cannot distinguish "never read" from "read, not persisted", the contract must make that boundary durable: register the request (arm) → read the full response body → persist the raw signed response bytes as a proof BEFORE interpreting them → then consequence; an OPEN child with no persisted response on relaunch = unobserved = CLEAN/UNKNOWN; with a persisted response but no consequence = replay the interpretation from the stored bytes (no loss). If Astra reads the bounded ruling as NOT covering a briefly-received-but-unpersisted revocation, that is the one place an owner question could arise — say so explicitly rather than silently choosing 18. (2) SIGN-OUT ARM CUT — "pre-arm before rendering the final Sign out action" arms the moment settings opens; Counterexample C: open settings, take a phone call, iOS kills the app → relaunch → OPEN → 18 for a user who never intended to sign out. Specify: arm on the FIRST tap of Sign out (two-step control), enable the final Confirm only after the arm's oncomplete, Cancel = durable close, and the relaunch resolution for an OPEN sign-out child without outcome = 17 (sign in again), never 18 — the intent belongs to the user, not the server. (3) OBSERVED BOUNDARY AND CLOSING — define "observed" as the response body fully read and parsed; before that an abort leaves the child unobserved; `observe()` after closing has begun must be REFUSED and leave the child UNRESOLVED (never dropped — dropping read negative knowledge is the loss the fence exists to prevent); close waits for every child to be terminal or aborted-before-read; a late response to a closed handle is dropped as stale by identity, never applied. (4) DURABLE GUARD SCHEMA — the frame's one guard byte cannot carry several concurrent children of different kinds; define the guard PROOF in the body {version, rootId, scope, sessionEpoch, cause, closingBegun, children:[{id, kind, source, requestIdentity/opId, registeredAtRevision, state: registered|observed|resolved, outcome?, responseProofRef?}]} with guardRef = its digest and the frame byte as the summary (OPEN iff any child unresolved); a NON-OWNER commit (another context's short local write) must carry guardRef byte-for-byte — test: a non-owner commit that changes guardRef is refused; state the cost plainly: every arm/outcome/close is a full-generation reseal, so arm ONCE per drain cycle with the child list, never per request. (5) OTHER CONTEXTS — publish the platform reality with a cited source before designing multi-context recovery: on iOS a Home Screen web app has its own storage container separate from Safari tabs (cowork's recollection; pin the WebKit source), so the installed app has one window and no same-origin tab sharing its IndexedDB; where tabs do exist (desktop, dev), use the Web Locks API for owner liveness — the user agent releases a held lock when the context dies, which is the authoritative "old observer ended" signal the proposal says heartbeat silence cannot give; cite support before relying on it. (6) AUTH CONTAINMENT — Astra's primary-source finding stands (Clerk 6.31: polling:false / touchSession:false do not stop AuthCookieService's unconditional refresh/poll, the 1.5 s / 5 s SessionCookiePoller, tokenCache timers, the clerk:session_token channel, or signOut → handleUnauthenticated); the "no Clerk SDK in the enrolled Today context, narrow explicit FAPI fetch driven by the manager" candidate is acceptable to REVIEW only with an executed BARRIER: an instrumented boot that enumerates every timer, listener, BroadcastChannel and fetch registered in the enrolled context and fails on any not routed through the manager; sign-in UI on a separate non-enrolled route; a cross-tab sign-out delivered by Clerk's channel is an ingress source and belongs in the inventory (or is excluded by the barrier); production CORS/CSRF/challenges/account switch/cancel-drain are not assumed solved (as Astra states) and wait for W4's real Clerk instance. (7) FIRST EXECUTABLE PROOF — keep the proposal's list and add: relaunch after a kill at each cut of a request child (registered / response persisted / consequence persisted / closing), asserting the per-kind resolution of (1); the settings-open-then-kill case of (2) must come back CLEAN; a non-owner commit under OPEN preserves guardRef; and the ordinary CLEAN bounded restart control. ASTRA'S DISAGREEMENTS RECORDED AS RED, NOT RESOLVED (cowork concurs, nothing adopted, no owner question yet): (a) the point-1 "local-sample exception" is WITHDRAWN — a learned expiry/revocation/rejection/rollback lost on failed persistence is exactly the HARD knowledge-loss blocker of BRIEF-W6 v1.1 and is NOT the owner's unproved-elapsed-time exception; a killed local permission sample before its atomic frame commit is a knowledge loss the restart budget does not cover; (b) "no persisted response ⇒ unobserved" is WRONG when status/headers/auth callbacks were seen before the failed write — "observed" must be the FIRST informative cut, not "fully read and parsed", and the earlier cuts must be inventoried; (c) an OPEN sign-out child before Confirm is not independently known intent — 17 cannot be assumed from Confirm never pressed; exact earliest-intent semantics and a false-positive-vs-unknown report are required; the ambiguous no-response case stays 18-until-re-proven and the C1 (offline availability) conflict is preserved as a formal unresolved contract item, not waved. PRIMARY EVIDENCE FOR POINT 5: Web Locks — the W3C spec releases every lock held by an agent when that agent terminates ("terminate remaining locks and requests") and scopes locks to agents sharing a storage bucket; WebKit's Safari 15.4 post: "Another new mechanism supported in WebKit is the Web Locks API … from an origin in tabs, windows, iframes, and Workers"; iOS Home Screen web-app storage isolation: NOT found in the WebKit Web Push post fetched — remains an unpinned fact, not to be relied on until a primary source is cited. ASTRA'S RAW-OBSERVATION CANDIDATE (durable raw record of a response or a local clock tuple + exact basis/obligation BEFORE any semantic evaluation; consequences computed after, replayable from the raw record; an OPEN local-raw obligation resolves OFFLINE from raw + basis) — cowork's assessment against the HARD rule, not the budget: sound in direction and consistent with the rule only under six executable conditions — (i) evaluation is a pure function of durable inputs (raw record, exact basis digest, fixed rule version) proven by replay tests, never of runtime epoch; (ii) the raw-commit FAILURE path is value-independent — the same state 3 and copy whatever the tuple, no comparator reachable, proven by a mutant that leaks the comparison into the failure path; (iii) negative consequences (17/19/20 latch) are monotone and applied from ANY unresolved raw observation regardless of basis staleness, positive permission only from the exactly matching basis; (iv) the final-cut sample taken inside the operation transaction is durably recorded on BOTH the publish and the control path (a refusal commits a control frame carrying the raw final sample), and the residual — an IndexedDB failure at the final cut loses that sample — is listed and examined under the sheet, not defined away; (v) the earlier-cut inventory is executed as an instrumented barrier: no comparator, status, header, expiry or auth-callback path reachable before the raw record's oncomplete, no SDK in the enrolled context; (vi) a reviewed observation-store schema bound to the basis digest with its own CAS, bounded count and post-resolution cleanup — the 352-byte frame carries only its digest. Sign-out under the same model (candidate, NOT adopted): the first tap is a raw intent observation recorded before any consequence; an unconfirmed intent found on relaunch resolves to ASK (re-present Confirm/Cancel, writes blocked until answered) — neither silent CLEAN nor assumed 17 — reported as unknown, not false positive.
